# Formats

Each thing on the rails has one format: a project, a data file's terms, a
method, a chain of checks, a deployment, and the `/translate` contract between
a translation service and what calls it. Each format is **versioned** (a
document names its format and version in `$schema`; a changed shape gets a new
version number, and the older one is still read) and **validated** against the
JSON Schema below.

Every tool reads these documents natively: the `champollion` CLI, `mt-eval`,
`nmt-forge` and the MCP server give the same verdict on the same file.

- `champollion validate [folder]` checks a project's files against these
  schemas: its `champollion.project.json`, every data sidecar
  (`<file>.champollion.json`), every `method.json`, its gate chains
  (`gates/*.json`) and its deployments (`deploy/*.json`). It reads no data
  file.
- `champollion upgrade [folder]` rewrites older shapes in the current format,
  losing nothing: a sidecar written before set/1 becomes set/1, and a key set/1
  does not know moves under `x-<key>`. An invalid sidecar is left for a person
  to fix. An older `method.json` is read as method/0 and left as it is.
  `--dry` says what would change and writes nothing.

Every document refuses keys it does not know, except keys that start with
`x-`: put your own notes there.

This page is generated from the schemas themselves, so every field on it is
exactly what the tools check.

| Format | What it is |
|---|---|
| [project/1](#project1) | Champollion project (project/1) |
| [set/1](#set1) | Data set sidecar (set/1) |
| [method/1](#method1) | method/1 — one translation method, as every tool reads it |
| [gate-chain/1](#gate-chain1) | gate-chain/1 — checks between a method's output and what ships |
| [deployment/1](#deployment1) | deployment/1 — what is deployed: one method, its gates, for one pair |
| [service-api/1](#service-api1) | service-api/1 — the /translate contract |

## project/1

**Champollion project (project/1)**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/project/1.json` — a document in this format says so in its `$schema` field. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/project.v1.schema.json`.

champollion.project.json — the root of a project on the rails. It holds DECISIONS only (what the project is for, its language pair, the defaults new data gets); facts about data live in each file's set/1 sidecar, events in the ledger. Written by `champollion new`; read by every tool. Unknown keys are refused; put your own notes under an `x-` key. A language, task or service project must name its pair (checked by the loader, which says so in words).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/project/1.json` | yes | Which schema this document follows. |
| `kind` | one of `language`, `task`, `service`, `app` | yes | language = build a translation method for a pair (internal dev); task = host a sealed shared task (a bounty); service = run a translation API; app = translate an app's or site's files. |
| `name` | string, not empty | yes | A human name for the project. |
| `pair` | object |  | The translation direction. Codes as the language cards name them (ISO 639-3 such as `eng`, `crk`; a private-use code such as `qaa` for a variety without one). |
| `pair.source` | string, matching `^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$` | yes |  |
| `pair.target` | string, matching `^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$` | yes |  |
| `pair.source_name` | string, not empty |  | The language's name as the people building this say it. Needed for a private-use code (qaa–qtz), which no language card names; otherwise read from the card. |
| `pair.target_name` | string, not empty |  | As source_name, for the target. |
| `purpose` | string |  | What the translations are for, in the community's words (e.g. 'school newsletter and classroom phrases'). Shown back to the people deciding, never sent anywhere. |
| `defaults` | object |  | What data added to this project gets when nobody says otherwise. The rails never invent an answer: `ask` makes the tools stop and ask. |
| `defaults.transmission` | one of `local-only`, `ask` |  | local-only = new files are marked so only a model on this machine may see them (the default `champollion new` writes); ask = ask for every file. |
| `defaults.training` | one of `allowed`, `not-allowed`, `ask` |  | Whether new data may be used to train a model here: allowed, not-allowed, or ask (the default). |
| `defaults.share_scores` | one of `never`, `ask` |  | Whether scores may ever be published: never, or ask (the default). Publishing is always an explicit step. |
| `created_with` | string |  | The tool and version that wrote this file (e.g. `champollion 0.6.0`). |
| `x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |

Keys not listed here are refused, except your own `x-` keys.

A **yes** in Required on a nested field (`a.b`) means: required whenever `a` is present.

## set/1

**Data set sidecar (set/1)**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/set/1.json` — a document in this format says so in its `$schema` field. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/set.v1.schema.json`.

`<file>.champollion.json` beside ANY data file (TSV, JSONL, JSON, text, a word list): who holds it, what it is for, and where its text may go. One format read by every tool (mt-eval, nmt-forge, the champollion CLI, the MCP server) — the steward sidecar, given a schema. A sidecar can only make a file STRICTER: it never loosens what a corpus envelope or a registry entry says. A sidecar written before set/1 (no `$schema`) is read as set/0 — the same fields, without the new ones — and stays valid. Unknown keys are refused; put your own notes under an `x-` key.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/set/1.json` |  | Which schema this sidecar follows. Absent on a sidecar written before set/1. |
| `transmission` | `local-only` |  | local-only = only a model on this machine may ever see the text; every tool refuses to send it anywhere. The only restriction value a sidecar sets. |
| `role` | one of `train`, `dev`, `test`, `sealed`, `input`, `resource` |  | What the file is for in the project. train = may be learned from; dev = tuning and model selection; test = the protected set scores are reported on; sealed = a test set no one outside its holders sees; input = text to translate (deployment: source only, nothing to score); resource = a dictionary, glossary or grammar the methods use. |
| `kind` | one of `parallel`, `monolingual`, `lexicon`, `grammar`, `glossary` |  | What the file holds: sentence pairs, one-language text, a word list or dictionary, grammar notes, or a terminology glossary. |
| `pair` | object |  | The direction the file's columns run (source → target), in the language cards' codes. |
| `pair.source` | string, matching `^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$` | yes |  |
| `pair.target` | string, matching `^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$` | yes |  |
| `fields` | object |  | Which column or JSON field holds which side, when the file does not use `source`/`target`. |
| `fields.source` | string, not empty |  |  |
| `fields.target` | string, not empty |  |  |
| `terms` | object |  | What the people who hold this data said about its use, recorded where every tool can read it. |
| `terms.training` | one of `allowed`, `not-allowed` |  | not-allowed = no tool may train a model on this file (enforced by nmt-forge's training mix); allowed = it may be learned from. |
| `terms.owner` | string, not empty |  | Who holds this data, in the holder's own words. |
| `terms.speakers` | string, not empty |  | Whose words the file holds — the people who said or wrote them — in the holder's own words (a family chat or an elder's notebooks hold other people's words). |
| `terms.speakers_agreed` | one of `yes`, `not-yet`, `some-said-no` |  | Whether the people whose words these are agreed to their use: yes; not-yet (not asked yet — no model may learn from it until they agree); some-said-no (no model may learn from this file — take their words out into another file first). |
| `terms.consent_record` | string, not empty |  | Path (relative to this file's folder) of the consent note that records who agreed to what, and when. |
| `id` | string, not empty |  | The registered corpus id (written by `champollion network register-corpus`); read verbatim, never re-derived. |
| `name` | string |  | The registered display name. |
| `license` | string |  | The licence the holder states (an SPDX id or a LicenseRef-\*). |
| `tier` | one of `local-only`, `private`, `sealed`, `public` |  | The registration tier `register-corpus` recorded. |
| `segment` | string |  | The corpus segment, as in a JSON envelope (e.g. `held_out`). |
| `sha256` | string, matching `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |  | SHA-256 of the data file when it was registered; a changed file no longer gets the card's id or grade. |
| `rows` | integer, ≥ 0 |  | Rows counted at registration. |
| `card` | string |  | Path (relative to this file's folder) of the corpora card registered for it. |
| `registeredAt` | string |  | When `register-corpus` registered the file (ISO 8601). |
| `derived_from` | string |  | The protected file this one was derived from (a split, a cleaned copy, a run's outputs); its marks were carried here. |
| `holders_agreed` | object |  | Who among the data's holders agreed that this file — the output of a method whose output is local-only — could be written where it is, outside its project, and when (written by `mt-eval translate --holders-agreed-by`). It loosens nothing: the file stays local-only for every tool. |
| `holders_agreed.by` | string, not empty | yes | Who agreed, as they were named. |
| `holders_agreed.date` | string, matching `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` |  | When it was recorded (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `written_by` | string |  | The tool command that wrote this sidecar. |
| `x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |

## method/1

**method/1 — one translation method, as every tool reads it**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/method/1.json` — a document in this format says so in its `$schema` field. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/method.v1.schema.json`.

A method's own description: what it is, how it runs (kind and that kind's one setting), what it translates, how it decodes, the card the leaderboard shows, and the measured evidence for it. Written as methods/&lt;id>/method.json in a project, by `nmt-forge export` into a model folder, by `mt-eval export` and `champollion serve --emit-manifest`; read by the champollion CLI, the eval harness and the MCP server natively. Before method/1 three unrelated documents were all called method.json (the CLI plugin manifest with `type`, the harness plugin manifest with `entry_point`, forge's export); the readers still accept those as method/0 with a warning. Kind-specific settings (engine, model, model_dir, dictionary, entry_point, service.endpoint) are required by the readers, with identical messages in both runtimes. Notes of your own go under x- keys.

## gate-chain/1

**gate-chain/1 — checks between a method's output and what ships**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/gate-chain/1.json` — a document in this format says so in its `$schema` field. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/gate-chain.v1.schema.json`.

An ordered list of gates the eval engine applies to every translated segment before it is scored or shipped (mt-eval run / test / translate --gates). People bring their own gates (founder, 2026-10-10): a gate of kind metric-threshold reads one per-segment value from a metric plugin — any plugin the harness loads, e.g. an FST validity check — and compares it with min and/or max. The first gate that refuses a segment decides what ships instead: drop (nothing), keep-source (the source text), flag (the output, marked) or fallback (the chain's fallback method's translation, if the gates accept it — else nothing). A segment the plugin cannot score is refused (no value). What is measured is what ships: the headline scores the gated output, the ungated score is reported beside it, and the refusal rate is a number of its own. Retrying a refused segment with the gate's reason comes later.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/gate-chain/1.json` | yes |  |
| `id` | string, matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$` | yes |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `gates` | array of objects (at least 1) | yes |  |
| `gates[].id` | string, matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$` | yes |  |
| `gates[].kind` | `metric-threshold` | yes |  |
| `gates[].metric` | string, not empty | yes | The metric plugin's name (MetricPlugin.name). |
| `gates[].field` | string, not empty | yes | The key in the plugin's per-segment result (a number, or true/false read as 1/0). |
| `gates[].min` | number |  | Refuse a segment whose value is below this. |
| `gates[].max` | number |  | Refuse a segment whose value is above this. |
| `gates[].on_refuse` | one of `drop`, `keep-source`, `flag`, `fallback` | yes |  |
| `gates[].description` | string |  |  |
| `gates[].x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |
| `fallback` | object |  | What translates a segment a gate refuses with on_refuse fallback: a method that runs on this machine (a dictionary: lexicon; a model: local-model), so nothing leaves it. Its output is checked by the same gates; refused again, nothing ships. For serving and translating only: a command that scores (mt-eval run / test) refuses a chain that falls back, because the score would be partly this method's and partly the fallback's under one name (founder, 2026-10-11) — measure the fallback as a method of its own. |
| `fallback.method` | string, not empty | yes |  |
| `fallback.model` | string |  | The dictionary (lexicon) or model (local-model) it runs. |
| `fallback.x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |
| `x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |

Keys not listed here are refused, except your own `x-` keys.

## deployment/1

**deployment/1 — what is deployed: one method, its gates, for one pair**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/deployment/1.json` — a document in this format says so in its `$schema` field. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/deployment.v1.schema.json`.

A deployment is the eval pipeline on source-only input (founder, 2026-10-09): the SAME document is tested on a test set (mt-eval run --deployment), run over a file (mt-eval translate --deployment) and served (mt-eval serve --deployment), so what was measured is what ships. Paths are relative to the project's root (where the rails run commands). It names no score: a measured number is a run result, kept with the run.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/deployment/1.json` | yes |  |

| `description` | string |  |  |
| `pair` | object | yes |  |
| `pair.source` | string, not empty | yes | The source language's code (ISO 639-3 or BCP-47). |
| `pair.target` | string, not empty | yes |  |
| `pair.target_script` | string, matching `^[A-Z][a-z]{3}$` |  | The script the output is written in (ISO 15924), for a gate that checks it — a server has no references to read it from. |
| `method` | object | yes | The method: an engine name (lexicon, local-model, …) or a method plugin's folder, with the model or dictionary it runs. Served only if it runs in this process. |
| `method.method` | string, not empty | yes |  |
| `method.model` | string |  | The model, model folder or dictionary file it runs. |
| `method.x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |
| `gates` | string, not empty |  | A gate-chain/1 file: every segment is gated before it ships (and before it is scored). |

| `x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |

## service-api/1

**service-api/1 — the /translate contract**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/service-api/1.json`. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/service-api.v1.schema.json`.

The one contract between a translation service and what calls it. Servers: nmt-forge serve, mt-eval serve, or anyone's (a method of kind `service`). Client: the champollion CLI's `api` method (sync, translate, serve). POST /translate takes a translate_request and answers 200 with a translate_response (207 when some keys failed, listed under `errors`), or an error_response (400 a request it cannot take, 401 a missing or wrong token, 404 an unknown route, 413 too large, 500 the method failed — never a partial answer). GET /health answers a health document. A field a server does not use is ignored, never refused. What a service writes can carry what it learned from: a server whose health says output_local_only true puts output_local_only true in the meta of every translate_response, and a client writes such output only where the data's holders agreed. Held to shared/test-fixtures/framework/service-api-vectors.json.

service-api/1 has no fields of its own: it defines the bodies the contract's requests and answers carry, each below.

### service-api/1: `translate_request`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keys` | object | yes | key → the source string to translate. Keys are the caller's (app message ids); values that are not non-empty strings come back under `errors`. |
| `source_locale` | string |  | Optional: the server refuses a language it does not translate from. |
| `target_locale` | string |  | Optional: the server refuses a language it does not translate into. |
| `method` | string |  | The method the caller expects; a server serving one method may ignore it. |
| `text_format` | `markdown` |  | Set for document text (Markdown); unset for app strings. A server that does not know it treats the text as plain. |
| `instructions` | object |  | key → a note for that key (plural form, a gate's retry reason). Sent only to a server declared to follow them (accepts_instructions). |
| `instructions.<key>` | string |  | One entry per key. |

### service-api/1: `translate_response`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `meta.model` | string |  |  |
| `meta.output_gates` | string |  |  |

| `meta.cost_usd` | number, ≥ 0 |  |  |

### service-api/1: `health`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `ok` | yes |  |
| `pair` | string, not empty | yes | source→target, as the server names them. |
| `output_gates` | string, not empty | yes | What the server checks in what it returns, said in words — 'none — …' when it checks nothing. |
| `output_local_only` | boolean or null | yes | true: what it writes may repeat sentences marked local-only, so it stays on this machine unless the data's holders agree. false: nothing it learned from is marked so. null: not known (said as such, never guessed). |
| `output_local_only_why` | string |  |  |
| `holders_agreed_by` | string or null |  | Who among the data's holders agreed that local-only output may be served on an address other machines reach; null when it is not (a local-only server is refused that address without it). |
| `model` | string or null |  |  |
| `method` | string |  |  |
